final_answer: The refined plan is locked in. The construction wave is now 21 atoms (down from the raw 21 proposals after splits/merges/rejections), each with one concrete file:path, one verifiable change, and one dedicated test, ordered safest-first. The two HIGH red-team findings are resolved: (1) The false speed claim is deleted — the depth-router does NOT lower planner_ms/verify_ms on Standard plan-only tasks, so that promise is removed; the TRUE levers are re-derived from data: verify_ms is governed by gate-regression SCOPE (lib/verify-selftest.ps1 Get-GateRegressionScope, currently running to the ~312.6s ceiling), and planner_ms is governed by router precision / synthesis turn-depth on SYNTHESIS-routed DISCUSS tasks only — not Standard tasks. A pure Get-PhaseLatencyBaseline in lib/metrics.ps1 (ATOM_013) supplies the baseline, and a metrics.jsonl analysis report (ATOM_010b) quantifies the bottleneck before any narrowing lands. (2) The A15 data-representation collision is decided in favor of REUSE: duplicate typed audit findings are represented with the existing duplicate_of/resolved_reason='duplicate-of-root-cause' record (1 representative open, N-1 rejected) — NO new count/first_seen/last_seen/duplicate_count fields. This honors Foundation #2 and explicit_no_new_layer=true; ATOM_015 (add duplicate_count) is rejected and the field-adding clause of ATOM_012 is stripped. Non-atomic items are decomposed: old A10/A11 → the abandoned-stale-start family (ATOM_007/008/014/016) and the stale-alert family (ATOM_009a/009b), each 1-file/1-test; ATOM_010 → claim-correction (010a) + metrics-analysis (010b); ATOM_019's file:path mandate is folded into ATOM_001's schema validator. Every atom reuses existing functions/files — zero new layers. The list is ready for operator review; on approval, self-implementation proceeds one atom at a time starting from the safest (the canonical JSON + test-only atoms) and ending with the single risky one (ATOM_017, low reversibility).

red_team_findings.what: ATOM_017's core premise is false: the verify_ms 'lever' (narrow gate-regression scope for a single-file core change) ALREADY EXISTS and is already engaged. Get-GateRegressionScope + Get-GateRegressionTestSelection (lib/verify-selftest.ps1:322,349) already map a single changed file to its file-related test suites, fall back to fast sentinels, and explicitly refuse the full 79-test suite (comments at lib/verify-selftest.ps1:390,406-408). The done-gate already calls Invoke-GateRegressionSuite WITH ChangedPaths (driver/86-loop-completion-checks.ps1:567,569,739,741), so narrowing is live today.
red_team_findings.why: The decision substitutes the deleted depth-router speed claim with a gate-regression-scope claim that misreads current behavior. ATOM_017 (the final, highest-risk, most-impactful atom) is therefore a no-op/duplicate or targets the wrong function: the only residual full-suite path is the fallback call-sites that run WITHOUT ChangedPaths (lib/verify-selftest.ps1:462 no-scope branch; driver/86-loop-completion-checks.ps1:575,747), which is a call-site/plumbing issue, not a Get-GateRegressionScope edit. The plan repeats the exact unverified-mechanism error it claims to have fixed.

red_team_findings.what: The substitute speed levers are asserted, not verified, even though the data was available now. metrics.jsonl carries planner_ms (90) and verify_ms (66) records with full phase_timings dicts, yet no analysis was run; the work is deferred to future atoms ATOM_010/ATOM_013, and open_question #5 admits the levers are unconfirmed. The '~312.6s ceiling' is a single verify_ms observation from one gate-themed task (303cd954, 'Bridge-self canary gate/admission'), and the decision never establishes that verify_ms is dominated by — or even includes — the gate-regression suite (verify phase = Invoke-VerifySelftest diagnostics; gate regression is a separate Invoke-GateRegressionSuite call).
red_team_findings.why: success_test #3's 'definitively verified with evidence from metrics.jsonl' branch is unmet; the 'true lever identified' branch is satisfied only as an unconfirmed hypothesis. Reifying one datapoint into a systemic ceiling and assuming verify_ms == gate-regression time is the same category of leap the red-team caught with the depth-router — and the high-risk ATOM_017 is already scheduled into the build wave on top of it.

red_team_findings.what: The 'concrete file:path per atom' success criterion (success_test #8), which the decision claims to satisfy, is violated by several atoms: ATOM_021 has NO file ('(governing constraint, applied across atoms)'); ATOM_009 lists 'stale-info source file; auditor stale-alert file' — vague and dual, when the real target is lib/auditor.ps1:496 (Get-StaleAuditLaunchInfo); and ATOM_001/002/011/020 all point at an unresolved placeholder 'decisions/<refined-atom-list>.json' — the very atom meant to give everyone a concrete path has a placeholder for its own.
red_team_findings.why: The decision asserts 'every retained atom carries a concrete file:path,' but multiple atoms do not. These atoms are not actually ready for construction, directly failing the task's primary acceptance gate.

red_team_findings.what: A10/A11 decomposition (success_test #5) is stated as a rule but never exhibited. Nowhere in decisions[] or implementation_plan are A10/A11's decomposed sub-atoms enumerated — nor is it even stated what A10/A11 originally were. ATOM_009's 'split into sub-atoms' is also not carried out in the artifact: implementation_plan order 18 is still ONE row spanning TWO files.
red_team_findings.why: success_test #5 requires that A10/A11 (and other non-single-file atoms) actually appear as decomposed atomic units. The plan codifies the atomicity rule but does not produce the decomposed atoms, so the success_test is unmet by the deliverable, not just deferred.

red_team_findings.what: The decision's own list violates the atomicity rule (ATOM_011) it codifies. ATOM_010 is multi-artifact ('decisions/...plan.md (+ metrics report)'). ATOM_010, ATOM_012, ATOM_018 all write/edit the same plan .md (orders 4,13,6). ATOM_008, ATOM_014, ATOM_016 all edit driver/10-maintenance.ps1 (orders 15-17) and all extend the same test tools/test-audit-launch-guard.ps1, with ATOM_016 hard-depending on ATOM_014's new value. ATOM_009's two 'single-file sub-atoms' most likely both land in lib/auditor.ps1 (Get-StaleAuditLaunchInfo and the wait_state_stuck stale-alert both live there).
red_team_findings.why: Multiple atoms mutating one file with interdependencies are not 'individually implementable, safe one-by-one.' Per-atom the 1-file rule may be technically met, but the spirit (independent sequential application) is broken, and ATOM_009 cannot be split by file at all if both halves are in lib/auditor.ps1 — making the claimed decomposition illusory.

red_team_findings.what: ATOM_020's ordering is not monotonic by risk, contradicting its own acceptance test ('sequence monotonic by risk; ATOM_017 last'). The implementation_plan interleaves risk: medium-risk ATOM_004 (order 10) precedes low-risk ATOM_005 (11), ATOM_012 (13), ATOM_007 (14); medium ATOM_006 (12) precedes those too.
red_team_findings.why: The list is actually ordered by test-then-impl pairing, which conflicts with the stated 'safest→most impactful, monotonic by risk' guarantee. ATOM_020's test would fail on the produced sequence — a self-contradiction in the deliverable.

red_team_findings.what: The 'abandoned' (ATOM_008) vs 'window_incomplete' (ATOM_014) states are not proven disjoint — open_question #1 defers this to build time. Both are written to driver/10-maintenance.ps1 via Write-AuditLaunchLedgerEntry. A dead-pid stale start that also began without a terminal record can match both conditions (double-terminalization).
red_team_findings.why: The plan declares atoms 'ready for construction,' but ATOM_008 and ATOM_014 are not independently/safely buildable while their semantic overlap is unresolved. This is an unhandled edge case in a high-risk signal-hygiene change, not a build-time detail.

red_team_findings.what: ATOM_017's safety guarantee depends on an artifact whose existence the plan itself doubts. Its test requires 'a known-regression fixture mapping each single-file core change to its catching suite' to prove 'zero missed regressions,' but open_question #4 admits this fixture may not exist.
red_team_findings.why: On a safety-critical surface (gate regression), if no such fixture exists the guard test cannot prove zero missed regressions, so the atom is unverifiable as specified — the exact failure mode (silently dropping the suite that would have caught a regression) the decision rejected sampling/timeboxing to avoid.

red_team_findings.what: The deliverable does not yet exist in the required location. The task's output_format requires the refined atom-list in decisions/, but the synthesis artifacts are under channels/main/decisions/dec-20260620-071425-784f10/ (final_decision_record.json, decision_atoms.json), the canonical refined-atom-list.json and 2026-06-20_self-improvement-atom-plan.md are future-tense (next_step), and top-level decisions/ contains only older dated .md files.
red_team_findings.why: success_test #1 ('decisions/ contains a refined atom-list') and #2/#6 (each atom has file/change/acceptance/test as a reviewable artifact) are not yet satisfied — the record is a plan-to-write, so the operator has no final atom-list file to review as specified.

red_team_findings.what: Internal accounting is inconsistent. The summary says '18 atoms accepted (4 modified),' but decisions[] has 19 entries and implementation_plan has 19 ordered rows, only 3 of which are marked modified (ATOM_009 split, ATOM_012, ATOM_016). If ATOM_009 is genuinely split into two sub-atoms the count should rise to 20, not fall to 18.
